description:
Title: Introduce chaotic prefetch fuzz runner and occupancy chronicle exporter

Motivation: We've been lacking a compact harness that intentionally perturbs prefetch/priming behavior and memory pressure while also producing a compact, kernel-aligned occupancy timeline that operators can use to diagnose burst-related inefficiencies. Existing runners either focus on large-scale replay fidelity or microbench kernels; this PR bridges the gap with a mid-weight fuzz runner that can run in CI and on our perf lab, plus an 'occupancy chronicle' exporter that converts GPU occupancy kernels and KV-cache priming events into a time-aligned heatmap JSON suitable for downstream visualization and regression detection.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a new CLI runner (cmd/fuzz-runner) that executes configurable sequences of: primer requests, variable prefetch delays, injected concurrency spikes, and synthetic memory pressure events. The runner supports deterministic seeds for reproducibility and a stochastic mode for exploration.
- Introduces an occupancy chronicle exporter (telemetry/exporters/occupancy_chronicle.go) which samples per-kernel occupancy metrics and maps them to primer/serving events; output is a compact gzip JSON (occupancy_chronicle_v1) with metadata to correlate with flamegraphs and scheduler traces.
- Adds a small calibration harness (bench/orchestrator/calibrator.go) that maps synthetic primer strength to expected KV-cache hit ratios on our mini-cluster; used by the runner to auto-tune primers for targeted hit-rate bands.
- New YAML workload examples (configs/synthetic/chaotic-prefetch.yaml) and a minimal local visualization script (tools/chronicle_viewer.py) to render ASCII and PNG heatmaps for quick triage.
- CI: lightweight smoke job (ci/perf-jobs/fuzz-smoke.yml) that runs a short deterministic sequence to detect regressions and verify exporter format; runs under the existing perf test matrix.

Design notes:
- The runner exposes a DSL that describes phases (prime, spike, idle, contention) and per-phase parameters (concurrency, inter-request jitter, prefetch_delay_ms). This keeps experiments reproducible while allowing quick fuzz compositions.
- Occupancy chronicle aligns metrics by wall-clock and by request-id; we include both to make off-cluster correlation straightforward. The JSON schema intentionally keeps kernel names, SM occupancy, and event pointers small to avoid extremely large artifacts when fuzzing for long durations.
- We intentionally avoided deep coupling with the existing flamegraph exporter; instead the chronicle provides stable anchors (event IDs/timestamps) that the flamegraph pipeline can consume to annotate traces.

Files changed (high-level):
- cmd/fuzz-runner/main.go (new) — CLI and runner lifecycle
- bench/orchestrator/calibrator.go (new) — primer strength calibrator
- bench/runner/chaotic_engine.go (new) — core phase engine and injectors
- telemetry/exporters/occupancy_chronicle.go (new) — sampler + serializer
- configs/synthetic/chaotic-prefetch.yaml (new) — example workload sets
- tools/chronicle_viewer.py (new) — local visualization helper
- ci/perf-jobs/fuzz-smoke.yml (new) — CI smoke test

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for the calibrator and serializer included (tests/calibrator_test.go, tests/chronicle_serializer_test.go).
- Ran full fuzz suite on the perf lab (8 runs with deterministic seeds) and validated that occupancy_chronicle outputs match manually inspected nvprof traces for sample workloads.
- CI smoke job is green on every run in this PR after the second commit; the initial failure was due to a race in the sampler that was fixed by adding a small lock and a stable sampling window.

CI summary:
- go test ./...: pass
- lint: pass (go vet + golangci-lint)
- perf-smoke (ci/perf-jobs): pass (deterministic run)
- e2e on mini-cluster: manual run by reviewer (see review conversation) — pass

Review conversation (high level):
- Carlos Rivera: Asked for clarifications about the sampling frequency and possible CPU overhead of the sampler. Also requested a guarantee that chronicle JSONs stay under 10MB by default.
  - Author reply (Maya): Default sampling reduced to 100ms and serializer switched to per-page deltas; added gzip on write. DOCS callout added.
- Priya Nair: Asked for API compatibility with existing flamegraph annotations and suggested adding a slight schema version field.
  - Author: Added occupancy_chronicle_v1 schemaVersion and example consumer snippet in docs/bench/README.md.
- Liam O'Connor: Requested a CI budget limit and fallback behavior when sampler fails to acquire metrics; suggested an opt-out flag for the mini-cluster to avoid noisy artifacts.
  - Author: Added --skip-sampler flag and made CI smoke run under --skip-sampler=false explicitly. Added retries for metric collection.

Merge notes: Squash-and-merge after addressing racy sampler; small follow-up commit added to tighten serializer memory usage.

How to use (quick):
1) Install: go build ./cmd/fuzz-runner
2) Run a deterministic smoke: ./fuzz-runner -config configs/synthetic/chaotic-prefetch.yaml -seed 42 -out out/chronicle.json.gz
3) View: python tools/chronicle_viewer.py out/chronicle.json.gz --render png

Why this matters: The new runner lets SREs and perf engineers cheaply explore primer/kv-cache sensitivity and produce a compact artifact (occupancy chronicle) that ties kernel occupancy to request phases. This unlocks faster triage of microbursts and prefetch inefficiencies without full-blown profilers on every run.
review_comments: Carlos Rivera: How expensive is the sampler at 10Hz? Can we bound CPU usage?
Maya Chen: Reduced default to 10Hz->10Hz was initial; changed default to 10Hz->100ms (10Hz) and implemented per-page delta writes + gzip to keep artifact size manageable.
Priya Nair: Please include schema versioning and an example consumer.
Maya Chen: Added schemaVersion field and consumer snippet in docs/bench/README.md.
Liam O'Connor: Add CI cap and opt-out for noisy sampler in mini-cluster. Also add retry logic on sampling.
Maya Chen: Added --skip-sampler flag; CI sets explicit flag. Added retry/backoff to metric collector to avoid transient failures.
